findings.reason: The existing source and both original-resolution tiles have no illustration. A pair of degree-one hat splines concretely clarifies overlapping compact supports and local partition of unity, relationships that the long general recurrence proof leaves spatially implicit. A specific nonuniform clamped knot example avoids implying general equal spacing or repeated-knot continuity.
findings.action: Added a final Remarks paragraph and native TikZ graph of B2 and B3 for p=1, xi=(0,0,1,3,4,4), highlighting [1,3) and their unit sum.

diagram_math_checks.justification: In def-b-spline-space-and-basis take p=1, n=4, a=0, b=4. Six knots (0,0,1,3,4,4) are clamped, interior multiplicities are one, and xi_j<xi_(j+2) for j=1,2,3,4. Nonuniform gaps 1,2,1 are drawn proportionally.

The supplier recurrence [F1] gives B_(2,1,xi)=x on [0,1), (3-x)/2 on [1,3), and zero outside [0,3]; its graph is (0,0)-(1,1)-(3,0). It gives B_(3,1,xi)=(x-1)/2 on [1,3), 4-x on [3,4], and zero outside [1,4]; its graph is (1,0)-(3,1)-(4,0). These are precisely the two colored paths. Supports denote closed supports, including the zero-valued endpoints.

The highlighted cell is [xi_3,xi_4)=[1,3), m=3. The active index range m-p through m is 2 through 3. The other two basis splines are supported on [0,1] and [3,4], so vanish on [1,3). On that cell (3-x)/2+(x-1)/2=1, matching the dashed unit-height segment and label, and the theorem step 4.1.

Both interior knots 1 and 3 have multiplicity mu=1=p, so C^(p-mu)=C^0 agrees with the continuous hat vertices, as asserted in the Statement and step 4.2. The caption explicitly excludes an inference about multiplicity p+1. The graph illustrates this concrete example only; no maps, crossings, or commutativity claims are asserted.
